statements.notes: Follow this workflow instead of default or built-in approaches.
statements.quote: **This workflow OVERRIDES all other built-in workflows.** When resolving a reported issue in an existing repository, follow this workflow rather than any default approach.

statements.notes: All five stages must run in sequence; can be checked through the existence of all five artifacts.
statements.quote: **The pipeline is fixed. Every stage always executes, in order.**

statements.notes: No stage may be skipped or adapted.
statements.quote: There is no stage selection, no depth selection, and no adaptive planning.

statements.notes: Read the rule detail file first in each stage.
statements.quote: Load that file as the first step of the stage

statements.notes: The stage is executed according to its rule detail file.
statements.quote: and execute the stage from it.

statements.notes: Ordered list of candidate directories; use the first one that exists.
statements.quote: Check these paths in order and use the first one that exists, regardless of which IDE or setup method was used: - `rule-details/` ... - `.swe-bench-pro/rule-details/` - `.claude/swe-bench-pro-workflow/rule-details/`
**Load one file at a time, immediately before its stage.**

statements.notes: No reading ahead; can be checked by comparing the order of reads and artifact writes in the trace.
statements.quote: Do NOT read a stage's rule detail file until the previous stage's Completion Criteria are met.

statements.notes: Results go in a file, not in chat.
statements.quote: **Every stage ends by writing its result to a file**, in the format its rule detail file specifies — not as chat output.

statements.notes: /tmp/swe-bench-pro/0N-<name>.md
statements.quote: **Artifact path**: `/tmp/swe-bench-pro/` + the stage's rule detail filename. Stage 1 writes `/tmp/swe-bench-pro/01-reverse-engineering.md`; Stage 5 writes `/tmp/swe-bench-pro/05-build-and-test.md`.
`mkdir -p` the directory before the first write.

statements.notes: Implied: no workflow artifact appears in the repository diff.
statements.quote: It sits outside the repository, so no artifact can reach the final diff.

statements.notes: Each artifact is written once, in full.
statements.quote: **One write, full content, at the end of the stage**, after its Completion Criteria are met.

statements.notes: Placeholders can be detected, e.g. TBD or <...>.
statements.quote: No appends, no placeholder to fill in later
**Never rewrite an earlier stage's artifact.**
A later stage that contradicts an earlier one records that in its own artifact — as a deviation, a correction, or a pre-existing failure

statements.notes: Headings must not be renamed or left out.
statements.quote: **Keep the prescribed skeleton exactly** — frontmatter keys, `##` headings, field prefixes.

statements.notes: The keys are stage (1-5) and name (reverse-engineering | requirements-analysis | code-generation-planning | code-generation-generation | build-and-test), from the fenced block at lines 33-38.
statements.quote: **Frontmatter is these two keys and no others:**

statements.notes: Unresolved work is recorded only in the Stage 5 Outstanding Failures section.
statements.quote: Unresolved work goes under Outstanding Failures in the Stage 5 artifact, and nowhere else.

statements.notes: Implied: artifacts carry no status or completion fields.
statements.quote: The artifact's existence is what states the stage finished.
**Do not re-read an artifact you can still see.**

statements.notes: Requirement IDs and step numbers must stay consistent across artifacts.
statements.quote: Quote identifiers — `R1`, step numbers, full paths — verbatim, never renumbered or paraphrased

statements.notes: Re-reading is allowed only for recovery.
statements.quote: **Read an artifact only to recover**, when an earlier stage's content is no longer visible because output was truncated or history was compacted
**No stage returns to an earlier stage.**

statements.notes: Applies to plan errors found in Stage 4 and fixes made in Stage 5.
statements.quote: it is handled inside the stage where it surfaced and the deviation is recorded in that stage's artifact.
**Consumes**: Task description
Load all steps from `01-reverse-engineering.md`
Execute them: identify the affected scope
determine the build and targeted test commands
locate and read the existing covering tests

statements.notes: Tests must run before any source edit; can be checked through the order of tool calls.
statements.quote: **MANDATORY**: Record the baseline pass/fail state by executing those tests **before any source file is modified**
Verify the Completion Criteria in that file are met
Write `/tmp/swe-bench-pro/01-reverse-engineering.md`

statements.notes: Must include paths, the owning module and the language/framework.
statements.quote: Affected Scope (paths, owning module, language/framework)
Build & Test Commands
Existing Tests
Baseline
Proceed to Stage 2
**This stage must run first because of the baseline.**

statements.notes: Stage 5 must compare its results against the Stage 1 Baseline.
statements.quote: It is recorded before any modification and consumed in Stage 5.
